title: Greek junta
capsule: The Greek military junta ('regime of the colonels') seized power on 21 April 1967 when Georgios Papadopoulos, Stylianos Pattakos, and Nikolaos Makarezos deployed armor through Athens using a NATO contingency plan as cover, arresting thousands of politicians hours before scheduled elections. The regime suspended the constitution, abolished political parties, imposed censorship, and practiced systematic torture; King Constantine II's counter-coup in December 1967 failed and sent him into exile in Rome. Dimitrios Ioannidis overthrew Papadopoulos in November 1973, and in July 1974 engineered a coup against Cypriot president Makarios III that triggered Turkish military intervention in Cyprus, collapsing the junta's credibility; civilian rule was restored under Konstantinos Karamanlis on 24 July 1974.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territory is simply the modern Greek state during this period and is unambiguously mapped; the Wikidata end-date of 1976 likely reflects the conclusion of junta trials and formal constitutional consolidation rather than the 1974 handover itself.
